HGV training

HGV training

Category C, Category C+E and Driver CPC. This page compares the routes. It does not confirm eligibility, a price or a course length.

Enquire nowWhich licence?

01632 960214 is an example number. Bristol, Taunton and Exeter are example bases.

Licence comparison

Three routes. Each has its own page, so this overview stays a comparison.

  • Category C

    Rigid goods vehicles such as box wagons, tippers, flatbeds and similar lorries

    A category B car licence is the usual starting point

  • Category C+E

    Articulated goods vehicles

    Category C is the usual entitlement held before C+E training

  • Driver CPC

    Periodic hours towards a Driver Qualification Card

    A professional lorry or bus entitlement is the usual starting point for periodic training

Which licence is right for me?

  • Category CPeople who want to drive a rigid goods vehicle over 3.5 tonnes. A category B car licence is the usual starting point. Medical and theory steps sit alongside the practical training.
  • Category C+EDrivers who already hold Category C and need to add the trailer entitlement.
  • Driver CPCProfessional lorry and bus drivers. Some work is exempt, and that depends on the job. Check current official guidance, or ask when you enquire, before you book.

Training pathway

The same sequence, whichever of the three routes you are on.

  1. Say what you want to drive

    Category C, Category C+E, Driver CPC, or one of the further courses. If you are not sure, say so.

  2. Check the licence you hold

    The current entitlement decides the medical, theory and practical steps. Nothing on this site confirms that a particular person qualifies.

  3. Train at the base that offers it

    Each course lists the example bases where it runs. A base does not list a course it does not offer.

  4. Prepare for the next step

    That may be a practical test or periodic training hours. How booking works is explained when you enquire. No result is claimed here.

Medical, theory, practical training and the test

  1. Medical

    A medical report is normally required before a lorry practical test. The current rules depend on the driver. This site does not confirm that anyone will pass.

  2. Theory

    Theory tests sit alongside time in the vehicle for a first lorry licence. Which tests apply depends on the entitlement being taken.

  3. Practical training

    Yard manoeuvres and road driving, in the kind of vehicle the course is for. No timetable is published here.

  4. Practical test

    The test covers vehicle control and driving on the road. Test content is set officially. This site does not claim a pass.

Questions

Which licence do I need?

Category C is the usual route onto a rigid lorry. Category C+E adds a trailer. Driver CPC is the professional qualification, not a vehicle category. The HGV training page compares them.

Do you publish prices?

No fee is listed. Ask for a quote for the course you want. Medicals, theory tests and the practical test are separate where they apply.

What is the difference between Category C and Category C+E?

Category C is the rigid lorry entitlement. Category C+E adds a trailer, for articulated lorries and drawbar outfits. C+E training normally follows Category C.

Is Driver CPC the same as an HGV licence?

No. Category C and Category C+E are vehicle entitlements. Driver CPC is a professional qualification for drivers who need a Driver Qualification Card. Operator CPC is different again: it is for transport managers.

Can this site tell me if I am eligible?

No. It is general guidance. The licence you hold is checked when you enquire.

Do I need a medical?

A medical report is normally required before a lorry practical test. Whether it applies to you depends on the entitlement and on current DVLA rules. This site does not confirm a medical result.
